svg.title: The fundamental plane of a lunar occultation
svg.desc: The fundamental plane seen along the line from the star. The Earth is a circle of unit radius with x running east and y running north from its centre. A straight track, rising gently from left to right, crosses near the top of the Earth's disc; it is the path of the centre of the Moon's shadow. Three circles of radius k are drawn on the track, at one hour before conjunction, at conjunction and one hour after; the middle one is solid and the other two are dashed. Two dotted lines parallel to the track, one above and one below, bound the band the circle sweeps. The lower line cuts across the Earth's disc and is labelled southern limit; the upper line lies wholly off the disc and is labelled northern limit. A vertical dimension on the left marks Y, the height of the track above the Earth's centre at conjunction, and an arrow inside the middle circle marks its radius k.
svg.text: Schematic from the elements of ES 1961 Example 10.2: Y = +0.9753, x′ = +0.6046, y′ = +0.0543, k = 0.2725.
The Earth's rotation is not drawn, so the band shows the shadow's sweep on the plane, not the zone on the ground.
